clue.text: Repaired her Nissan, working with double horsepower?

indicators.note: a repaired car has been put back together, so these letters are rebuilt into a new order

explanation.surface: A motorist fixes their Nissan, which now runs as if it had twice the horsepower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repaired' rearranges the letters of HER NISSAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to be in harness is to be at work, and literally describes a pair of horses yoked together.

clue.text: Popular fine artist, till that's unbecoming

parts.note: popular means in, as in fashion
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
to till the soil is to dig it

explanation.surface: A well-liked artist working the land with a fine finish strikes someone as undignified.
explanation.walkthrough: IN FRA DIG is short for Latin infra dignitatem, beneath one's dignity.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something beneath one's dignity is unbecoming behaviour for a person of standing.

clue.text: Question about garden tool in country feature

indicators.note: about means the question word wraps round the tool

parts.note: how is a question word
an edger is a tool for trimming lawn edges

explanation.surface: Someone asks about a gardening implement when looking at a rural landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: rows of hedging bordering fields are a typical sight in the English countryside.

clue.text: Rearing mostly fruit

indicators.note: mostly means all of the word but its final letter

parts.note: rearing children is raising them

explanation.surface: Growing fruit, for the most part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the G from RAISING.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a dried grape is a kind of fruit.

clue.text: One succeeding might acquire this long vehicle

definitions.meaning: an heir succeeding to a title inherits the family lands and property
a car with a long body and a rear hatch, called a station wagon in the US

explanation.surface: An heir might come into this, or a big car.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: landed property passed on at death, and a British car body type.

clue.text: Criticism dismissed in project

parts.note: stick is informal British for criticism, as in giving someone stick
a batsman dismissed in cricket is out

explanation.surface: Harsh comments get thrown out in some scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to project is to protrude, jutting beyond a surface.

clue.text: Racket is put in hands of one criminal

indicators.note: put in the hands of means placed within the grasp of, so the word is goes inside
criminal suggests something bent or crooked, so the letters of one are jumbled

explanation.surface: A racketeering scheme is entrusted to a lone crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racket' suggests crime, but here it means din; 'criminal' scrambles the word one, which 'put in hands of' then wraps round.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a racket is a loud din or commotion.

clue.text: Break's arranged in northern extreme of America — here?

definitions.text: Break's arranged in northern extreme of America — here?

indicators.note: in means the shuffled letters sit between the other two pieces
the extreme of a word is its end letter, here the first
arranged means the letters are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A gap is set up at the northern edge of America, and the place in question might be here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' and 'in' do the work; the whole clue also points at a US state, so it reads as its own definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a midwestern US state, the place the clue's 'here' points to on a map of America.

clue.text: Whip up awareness in audience

indicators.note: an audience hears rather than reads, so the word is taken as spoken

parts.note: insight is a perceptive awareness

explanation.surface: Stir up understanding among the listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in audience' says INSIGHT is heard, giving the same sound spelt differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to whip up feeling in a crowd is to stir or provoke it.

clue.text: Show French wine in English church

indicators.note: in means the French word sits between the other letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
vin is French for wine

explanation.surface: A French wine is displayed in an English church.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to evince a feeling is to show or reveal it plainly.

clue.text: Trendy type of commercial record endlessly in paper

indicators.note: in means the advert and record sit within the newspaper

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper
an ad is a commercial

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a disc is a record

explanation.surface: A fashionable person's advert for a record runs in a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Financial Times is the crossword's usual 'paper'; 'endlessly' trims the record before 'in' places it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who follows every passing craze is a trend-chaser.

clue.text: Harmony shown by one playing instrument

parts.note: being in accord is being in harmony
I is the Roman numeral one
on means playing, as in a show being on

explanation.surface: A musician shows harmony while playing an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a squeezebox with bellows and keys is a musical instrument.

clue.text: Disorder as newspaper boss rejected series of products

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: ED is short for editor
a range is a line of related products

explanation.surface: Chaos follows when the editor turns down a product line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns ED into DE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to derange is to throw into confusion or disarray, a verb sense of disorder.

clue.text: Crowd disowning leader, part of drama that's offensive

indicators.note: disowning leader means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a mob is a crowd
a scene is a part of a play

explanation.surface: A crowd rejects its leader in a part of a play that offends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disowning leader' cuts MOB to OB.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something lewd or indecent is grossly offensive.

clue.text: Skip speech that's to be self-evident

parts.note: to skip a meal is to go without it
a saying is a piece of speech, a proverb

explanation.surface: Not bothering to make a speech because the point is obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something that needs no stating is obvious, plainly self-evident.

clue.text: Problem for agency manager, maybe, as a pattern

definitions.meaning: a temporary worker arriving late, a headache for whoever runs a staffing agency
a guide shape or model to copy from

explanation.surface: A worry for someone running an agency serves as a pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the answer as TEMP LATE: a temporary worker not on time.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a shaped guide used to reproduce a design is a pattern.

clue.text: Memorable event or cause

definitions.meaning: a reason or grounds, as in having no ... to complain

explanation.surface: A notable event, or the reason for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a special celebration, and a reason or grounds for doing something.

clue.text: Raise most of ship wrecked in body of water

indicators.note: a wrecked ship is broken up, so these letters are rearranged
most of means the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Salvagers raise most of a ship that went down at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' cuts SHIP to SHI; 'wrecked' rearranges RAISE plus SHI.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the sea between Britain and Ireland is a body of water.

clue.text: Grotesque spouter?

parts.note: a grotesque is a carved ugly figure, and this one spouts rainwater from a church roof

explanation.surface: An ugly windbag who will not stop talking.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a carved monster on a building that acts as a water spout.

clue.text: Raise I'm upset about, becoming like a ritual

parts.note: to tote is to carry or lift

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means overturned, here read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
C is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: Someone is upset about a raise, as if it were a ritual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns I'M into MI.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: relating to a revered emblem or sacred symbol, as in ritual worship.

clue.text: Junk diet Greek character's given up in boredom

indicators.note: to junk something is to scrap it, so these letters are broken up
given up in a down clue means turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: mu is a Greek letter

explanation.surface: Abandoning a diet of junk food out of boredom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Junk' rearranges DIET to TEDI; 'given up' turns MU into UM.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: dull, wearisome monotony is boredom.

clue.text: Conundrum in festival with time to the fore

indicators.note: to the fore means moved to the front of the word

parts.note: Easter is a Christian festival

explanation.surface: A puzzle at the spring festival, with the clock pushed forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the fore' moves the T of EASTER to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a tricky puzzle or brain-twister is a conundrum.

clue.text: This could be a regular breakfast item?

definitions.text: This could be a regular breakfast item?

parts.words: This could be a regular breakfast item?
parts.note: regular means a regular army member, and a strip of toast for dipping into an egg is a breakfast item

explanation.surface: Something you might eat at breakfast every day.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a finger of toast dipped in a boiled egg has a military nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses joined: a regular infantryman, and a strip of buttered toast at breakfast.

clue.text: Second diplomatic group ready for nightfall?

parts.note: UN is the United Nations
set means ready, as in ready, steady, go

explanation.surface: A second group of diplomats is prepared for the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Near-synonym: the setting of the sun marks the coming of dusk, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Detest swearing in case of ladette

indicators.note: in means the curse sits between the outer letters
case of means the outside letters of the word

parts.note: an oath is a swear word

explanation.surface: Hating the foul language of a rowdy young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: A ladette is British slang for a young woman behaving loutishly. 'case of' takes L and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to hate intensely is to detest.

clue.text: Sloth perhaps from Andes, idly meandering

indicators.note: meandering means wandering about, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A sloth ambling lazily through the Andes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sloth' looks like the animal, but here it is the vice.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: sloth, idleness, is one of the seven traditional cardinal vices.

clue.text: Meet son, say, fit after jogging

indicators.note: jogging means jolted about, so these letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Meeting a son who is fit after going for a run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jogging' rearranges SAY FIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to meet a requirement is to fulfil it.

clue.text: Drummer gently crushes 'Come Together'

indicators.note: crushes means the phrase squeezes the word within it

explanation.surface: A drummer plays the Beatles song softly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come Together' is a Beatles song, a decoy for the plain verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to combine or join into one is to come together.

clue.text: Comment about curiously read mass in foreign cathedral

indicators.note: about means the remark wraps round the other letters

parts.note: a note is a brief comment

indicators.note: curiously means oddly, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark about reading mass strangely in a cathedral abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curiously' scrambles read, and 'about' wraps the comment round that plus mass; 'foreign' points to Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Gothic church in Paris is a famous cathedral outside Britain.
